findings.passage: “Senate Bill 202 is yet another anti-voting omnibus bill. Like House Bill 531 and Senate Bill 241, it represents a blatant attempt to undermine our democracy, our voters, and our electoral process.
findings.note: Senate press office statement issued in her name as Legislative Black Caucus chair on the day SB 202 was signed. It does not mention ID rules directly.

findings.passage: There is no legitimate report, investigation, inquiry, or audit that uncovers any conspiracy to commit voter fraud or rig an election in favor of a candidate.
findings.note: Same statement; she says there is no evidence of voter fraud conspiracy. Related to the voter-fraud argument behind ID laws.

findings.passage: If successful, members of the Senate will prevent nonprofit organizations from mailing absentee ballot applications to voters, require an excuse for absentee balloting, end automatic voter registration when obtaining a state issued driver’s license or identification card, and end the use of ballot drop boxes, just to name a few.
findings.note: Senate press office statement in her name as caucus chair on a package of Senate voting bills; she lists ending automatic registration at the licence or ID card office among them.
